svg.title: Who writes the clock matters: three WSL2 situations from t = 0
svg.desc: Three side-by-side panels share one 0 to 120 second axis and one symmetric-log ppm scale from minus 100,000 to plus 100,000 ppm with the historical plus or minus 1000 ppm screen. Left, Ubuntu 24.04 with systemd-timesyncd enabled, measured on this host on 2026-09-24 against the guest's own raw clock: every 30 second window was outside the screen, between minus 55,089 and minus 49,693 ppm (rounded outward), about 5 percent slow, with forward CLOCK_REALTIME jumps of about +1.6 s at 31, 65 and 99 seconds; the 300 second run was minus 48,010.756 to minus 48,010.740 ppm and the kernel tick moved from 10000 to 9437. The Windows host clock was about 1.06 s behind NTP with the Windows Time service stopped. Middle, Ubuntu 24.04 after the timesyncd stop, the historical D4R2 series against Windows QPC: t = 0 is the window opening about 60 s after the confirmed stop with the unit still enabled; window 1 measured +26,665.299 to +26,724.999 ppm, outside the screen; windows 2 to 4 were within about plus or minus 33 ppm; the 120 second run was +6,661.607 to +6,676.217 ppm, still outside; tick 10833 before and 10000 later. Right, Ubuntu 26.04 fresh default with chrony running with -x, measured on the same host the same day: all ten 30 second windows inside the screen between minus 0.73 and minus 0.27 ppm (rounded outward), the 300 second run minus 0.535 to minus 0.511 ppm, no jumps, tick 10000 throughout. Who changes tick is not established. Summaries pop up as each 30 second window closes; motion is playback at ten times real time; with animation off the complete result is shown.
svg.text: Who writes the clock matters: three WSL2 situations from t = 0
How to read: one shared 0–120 s axis and one symmetric-log ppm scale; the three cursors move together at 10× real time.
Left and right: guest-side screens on one Windows host on 2026-09-24, fresh WSL boot, one distro at a time.
Middle: historical D4R2 against Windows QPC; t = 0 is ≈60 s after the confirmed stop. Every box is a committed enclosure.

g.text: t = 0 ≈ 60 s after the confirmed stop
same host, same day as the left panel
* running means are derived from the committed window enclosures, assuming equal 30 s windows; the 120 s run is the measured enclosure.
Left/right host: W32Time stopped, host clock ≈1.06 s behind NTP (not changed). Guest-side only; not a controlled ranking.
Who lowers tick (9437 here, 10833 in D4R2): not established. timesyncd's source excludes it; chrony was not running.
C1 remained INCONCLUSIVE · sources: docs/same-host-screens-2026-09-24.md, docs/timesyncd-investigation.md
